newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia signs $500 mln standby loan facility.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia signs $500 mln standby loan facility.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, said on Tuesday it had signed a $500 million standby loan facility with 40 international banks.
The eight-year standby loans with bullet repayments were fully revolving and carried an interest rate of 0.625 percent above the London interbank offered rate (Libor), it said.
The bank said the commitment fee was 0.3125 percent per annum and the management fee was a flat 0.65 percent.
The bank said the terms and conditions were similar to the previous standby loan signed in May last year in Singapore.
It said the loan was to keep an approximate amount of $2.0 billion as a cushion for possible increase in obligations or an unfavourable balance of payment positions.
The bank said Indonesia's economy was integrated into the world economy and sensitive to any disruption.
"Any event, either economic or non-economic, domestically or internationally, will affect the financial sector and hence economic stability," Bank Indonesia said.
"The standby facility is used as a cushion to solve potentially vulnerable and sudden capital outflow that would harm the balance of payments," it said.

Coordinating arrangers for the issue were Commerzbank Ltd, The Fuji Bank Ltd, The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, JP Morgan Securities Asia Ltd, Natwest Markets, Sanwa International Finance Ltd and the Tokyo-Mitsubishi International (HK) Ltd.

The central bank said 60 percent of the syndicate members were Japanese banks, while there were two banks from the United States, three from South Korea, five from Taiwan, two from Germany and one each from United Kingdom, France, Australia and Spain.
